notes: Page 2 shows only the robber minifigure being assembled (hat, head, torso, legs, brown backpack) plus a callout adding two green banknote tiles. The minifigure parts are not in the parts list or catalogue, so they are not recorded.
The two '100' banknote tiles go onto the robber's backpack, which is not in the parts list, so they have no resting edges (rests_on is empty for both).
The second minifigure, the police officer in a brown cap and tan shirt, is shown only as a finished figure. It adds nothing.
The output schema available here is the full-graph schema, not the per-page one (pieces, other_joins). The two tiles are therefore returned as parts b1 and b2 with no edges.
Step 1: the reddish brown 1 x 4 log is pressed onto one long edge of the reddish brown 2 x 4 plate. It rests on b3, and rests_on = [b3].
The image does not show which long row of the plate the log covers. I used row 1 (stud.1.1 to stud.1.4).
The schema available is the full-graph one, so only the parts and edges new on this page are returned. The ids continue from b2 on page 2.
Step 2: the reddish brown 4 x 4 cut-corner wedge plate is pressed onto the free studs of the 2 x 4 plate (b3). The log (b4) is on the other side of the plate. rests_on = [b3].

The picture does not show exactly which wedge studs overlap the plate. I assumed the wedge's full 4-stud edge row (row 1) sits over the plate's free row 2, studs 2.1 to 2.4. Treat this overlap as approximate.
Only the parts and edges new on this page are returned. The schema available is the full-graph one.
Step 3: the dark bluish gray 3 x 1 slope (b6) and the dark green 2 x 1 slope with bottom pin (b7) go onto the wedge plate (b5), beside the log. rests_on: b6 = [b5], b7 = [b5].

Step 4 has a '2x' box, so two reddish brown 1 x 2 plates are added (b8, b9). Only one is drawn. b8 is drawn spanning the stud on the gray slope (b6) and a stud on the log (b4), so rests_on = [b6, b4]. I placed b9 on the log's other two studs, rests_on = [b4]. Its position is a guess.
The exact wedge studs under the two slopes, and the exact log studs under the plates, are not clear from the images. The stud indices in the edges are approximate.
The bottom pin on the dark green slope (b7) is not used on this page, so there is no other_join for it.
Only the parts and edges new on this page are returned. The schema available is the full-graph one.
Step 5: the reddish brown 1 x 2 handle tile (b10) is pressed onto the top of the plate stack, with its handle pointing up. rests_on = [b8].
I assumed the tile covers both studs of plate b8. The image is small and does not show whether it also covers part of the other plate (b9), so b9 is not listed.
Only the parts and edges new on this page are returned. The schema available is the full-graph one.
Step 6: the lime round 1 x 1 plate (b11) is pressed onto a wedge stud beside the dark green slope. The exact stud is a guess (b5 stud.3.3). rests_on = [b5].
Step 6: the black 1L bar with clip (b12) is clipped onto the handle of the reddish brown handle tile (b10), with its bar pointing up. This is a clip join, not a resting join.
Step 7: the dark green 6 x 5 leaves (b13) are pushed onto the upright bar of b12. The plant's only catalogue port is bar.1, so I joined it bar.1 to bar.1.
Only the parts and edges new on this page are returned. The schema available is the full-graph one.
Page 8 shows the finished hideout (the brown base with the plant, the lime plate and the bar) next to the robber minifigure. It has no building step, so no pieces or joins are added.

Page 9 has no building step. The red arrow shows the plant (b13) swinging up on its clip bar to reveal the brown money bag with the banknotes (b1, b2) hidden underneath. The robber minifigure stands beside it.
The bag is the robber's backpack from page 2. It is a minifigure accessory that is not in the parts list, so it is not recorded as a part. No new pieces or joins are added.
Page 10 starts the ATV model. Step 1 places the dark bluish gray 2 x 6 brick (b14) as the first piece of the ATV. It rests on nothing, so rests_on = [] and there are no edges.
The ATV is a new, separate sub-model from the hideout built on pages 3 to 9. It has no joins to b1 to b13.

Step 2 (2x): two black 2 x 2 wheel-holder plates (b15, b16) are pressed onto the underside of the 2 x 6 brick (b14), one at each end. The brick sits on top of them, so each plate has rests_on = [] and b14 is the piece clutching them. The edges run from b14's anti-studs to the plates' studs. The wheel holders point outward on the sides.
Step 3 (2x): two dark blue mudguards (b17, b18) go on top of b14, one at each end, with the fenders over the wheel holders. rests_on: b17 = [b14], b18 = [b14].

The 2 x 4 mudguards cannot both fully overlap a 2 x 6 brick. I assumed each one clutches a 2 x 2 patch at its end: columns 1-2 for b17 and columns 5-6 for b18. I used the middle two of the mudguard's four anti-stud columns. These stud and anti-stud indices are approximate.
Only the parts and edges new on this page are returned. The schema available is the full-graph one.

Step 4 (2x): two white 1 x 1 plates with a vertical clip (b19, b20) are pressed onto the studs of one dark blue mudguard. The image shows the first already placed and the second being lowered right behind it, so both go on the same mudguard. rests_on: b19 = [b18], b20 = [b18].
I assumed that mudguard is b18, and that the studs are its outer pair (stud.1.2 and stud.2.2). The image does not make clear which mudguard or which studs, so these are approximate.
Only the parts and edges new on this page are returned. The schema available is the full-graph one.
Step 5 (2x): two more white clip plates (b21, b22) fill the remaining studs of the same mudguard (b18), so it now carries a 2 x 2 block of four clips. rests_on: b21 = [b18], b22 = [b18].
Step 6: the dark blue 1 x 2 grille tile (b23) is pressed onto the studs of two clip plates. The image does not show which pair, so I assumed b19 and b20. rests_on = [b19, b20].
Only the parts and edges new on this page are returned. The schema available is the full-graph one.

Step 7: the yellow 1 x 2 handle tile (b24) is pressed onto the studs of the two clip plates not covered by the grille tile, b21 and b22. rests_on = [b21, b22]. This is an inference from the previous page. The handle faces up.
Only the parts and edges new on this page are returned. The schema available is the full-graph one.

Step 8 (2x): each light sub-assembly is a Trans-Dark Blue round plate pressed onto a light bluish gray tap, with a Trans-Red round tile pressed onto the other end of the tap. Two are built: (b25, b27, b29) and (b26, b28, b30). The colours come from the parts list. The teal-looking parts in the image are the Trans-Dark Blue plates.

Each finished sub-assembly is then attached to the clip of one white clip plate. I assumed the tap's body is held in the clip, one on b19 and one on b20. This is a clip join. The image is small, so which clips are used is approximate.
The tap catalogue entry has only anti.1.1, so the joins to the tap's spout and body use a null port.
No rests_on entries apply to these pieces. Only the parts and edges new on this page are returned. The schema available is the full-graph one.

Step 9: a light bluish gray 1 x 2 side-handle plate (b31) and a white 1 x 2 jumper plate (b32) go onto the studs of the other dark blue mudguard (b17), the one without the clips. I assumed b31 covers the studs in row 1 and b32 the studs in row 2. rests_on: b31 = [b17], b32 = [b17].
The exact stud rows are approximate because the image is small.
Only the parts and edges new on this page are returned. The schema available is the full-graph one.

Step 10: the dark bluish gray bar holder with clip (b33) is pressed onto a free middle stud of the 2 x 6 brick (b14). I assumed stud.1.3, which the mudguards do not cover. The handlebars (b34) are then pushed into the bar holder. rests_on: b33 = [b14]. The handlebars are held by the holder, not resting on it.
Catalogue gaps: 11090 has no listed stud or anti-stud port, so the join from b33 to b14 uses a null port on the holder. The handlebars' pin.1 is joined to the holder's bar-holder.1 port.

Step 11: the white 'POLICE' slope (b35) goes onto the front mudguard, over the side-handle plate b31, with the white jumper plate b32 beside it. I assumed it clutches b31's two studs, so rests_on = [b31]. It could instead sit on b32 and b17. The image is unclear.
Only the parts and edges new on this page are returned. The schema available is the full-graph one.

Step 12: the front bumper sub-assembly is a black 1 x 2 plate with horizontal clips (b36) with two Trans-Yellow round plates (b37, b38, the headlights) on its studs. rests_on: b37 = [b36], b38 = [b36].

The sub-assembly is then swung onto the front of the car (red arrow). I assumed its two clips grip the two side handles of the light bluish gray handle plate b31, which is at the front. These are clip joins, not resting joins. The image does not show this clearly, so treat the attachment as approximate.
Only the parts and edges new on this page are returned. The schema available is the full-graph one.

Step 13 (4x): each light bluish gray wheel is pressed into a black tyre. The four wheel and tyre sets (b39 to b42 with b43 to b46) are then pushed onto the wheel-holder pins of the two black wheel-holder plates, two wheels per plate. b15 carries b39 and b40, and b16 carries b41 and b42. The wheels are on the sides, not resting on anything. The wheel-and-tyre joins are rigid. The wheel-to-plate joins are revolute.
The tyre has no ports in the catalogue, and the wheel-holder plate has no pin port, so those joins use a null port. The wheel's pin-hole.1 is named on the wheel side.
Which wheel goes on which side of each plate is not shown, so the b39 to b42 assignment is arbitrary.
Only the parts and edges new on this page are returned. The schema available is the full-graph one.

Step 14: the car is turned over. The black 1L bar with clip (b48) is fitted onto the end of the light bluish gray 3L bar (b49) to make an upright post, and the 3L bar is then clipped into a free white clip plate (b21) at the rear of the car. I assumed this post is a catch or pole for the handcuffs.
The handcuffs (b47) are clipped onto the other free white clip (b22). The handcuffs have no catalogue ports, so their port is null.
Which white clips these parts use is not clear from the image, so those two clip joins are approximate.
Only the parts and edges new on this page are returned. The schema available is the full-graph one.

Page 21 has no building step. It shows the finished ATV next to the police officer minifigure, who holds the pole (the 3L bar with the black clip, b48 and b49) with the red snake in its clip. The pole is shown removed from the car.
The red snake (lego-30115) is in the parts list but has not been placed in any step yet. It is not recorded here because no step adds it. The officer minifigure parts are not in the parts list.
No pieces or joins are added.
Page 22 is advertising for other LEGO City sets (60047, 60046, 60044, 60043, 60042, 60041). It has no building step, so no pieces or joins are added.
Page 24 is the back cover: a product-feedback promotion, trademark text and the booklet number 6109341. It has no building step, so no pieces or joins are added.
I did not receive page 23, so it is not recorded.
The red snake (lego-30115) from the parts list was never placed in any step I saw. It is shown held on the pole on page 21. Its attachment, if any, would have to come from a page I did not see.

Parts list fix: only one lego-48729b (black) exists, and it is b12 on the hideout. The top of the pole on page 20 is the dark bluish gray 1 x 1 clip tile (lego-15712). So b48 is re-typed from lego-48729b to lego-15712, Dark Bluish Gray. This b48 entry replaces the earlier one with the same id.
Replace the earlier edge b48 bar.1 to b49 bar.1 with the edge given here: b48 clip.1 holds the end of the 3L bar b49. lego-15712 has no bar port.

Parts list fix: the red snake (lego-30115) is added as b50. Page 21 shows it on top of the pole, so I joined it to the clip of b48 with a null port on the snake. The exact way it is held is an assumption.

Connectivity: the booklet builds two separate models. The hideout (b3 to b13) is built on pages 3 to 9, and the ATV (b14 onward) on pages 10 to 20. Page 10 starts a new model, and nothing physically joins the two, so the two groups stay separate.

The loose banknote tiles b1 and b2 were not joined to anything. They are the contents of the robber's backpack, which is a minifigure part not in the parts list. On page 9 the bag sits beside the sloped brick of the hideout. I added contact edges: b1 to b2, and both to the gray slope b6. This is approximate.
The pole (b49 and b48) and the snake (b50) are connected to the ATV through the clip joins to the white clip plates b21 and b22, so they are not separate groups.

The two groups are real. Set 60065 has two separate builds: the robber's hideout (pages 3 to 9) and the police ATV (pages 10 to 20). Page 10 opens with a new model picture and a fresh first brick, and no step joins the two. So I did not connect them, and the earlier graph stands unchanged.
The hideout group is b1 to b13, with the banknote tiles resting beside the sloped brick. The ATV group is b14 to b50, with the pole and snake clipped on.
Because nothing in the booklet joins the two models, any edge between them would be invented, so I added none.
